concepts.name: PMFBY: Genesis, Evolution and Replacement of Predecessor Schemes
key_dimensions: Schemes replaced by PMFBY: NAIS (National Agricultural Insurance Scheme) and MNAIS (Modified NAIS) — key distinctions from each
Year of launch (2016) and the policy vacuum it addressed vs. limitations of NAIS/MNAIS (actuarial vs. subsidized premium)
WBCIS (Weather Based Crop Insurance Scheme) — whether it was merged into PMFBY or runs parallel (UPSC trap: it runs parallel)
Restructured PMFBY post-2020 reforms — what changed and why (voluntary vs. mandatory shift)

concepts.name: Premium Structure and Subsidy Sharing under PMFBY
key_dimensions: Farmer-payable premium caps: Kharif (2%), Rabi (1.5%), Annual Commercial/Horticultural crops (5%) — fixed ceiling, not actuarial
Difference between actuarial premium rate and farmer-payable premium — government absorbs the balance
Premium subsidy sharing ratio between Centre and State: general states (50:50), NE states/hilly states (90:10) — UPSC trap on NE states
No upper cap on government premium subsidy — implication for fiscal burden and why states sometimes opt out

concepts.name: Mandatory vs. Voluntary Coverage — The 2020 Policy Shift
key_dimensions: Pre-2020: Compulsory for loanee farmers (KCC/crop loan holders); Post-2020: Voluntary for all including loanee farmers
Rationale for shift: moral hazard, farmer complaints of forced deductions, low claim satisfaction
Impact on enrollment numbers post-2020 — paradox of lower enrollment vs. policy intent of wider coverage
States that made it compulsory again at state level vs. Centre's voluntary stance — federal tension

concepts.name: Risks Covered and Excluded under PMFBY
key_dimensions: Covered risks: Prevented sowing, mid-season adversity, post-harvest losses (up to 14 days), localized calamities (hailstorm, landslide, inundation)
Excluded risks: War, nuclear risks, malicious damage, theft, preventable risks — UPSC trap on 'localized' vs. 'widespread' coverage mechanism difference
Post-harvest loss coverage — specific condition: only for crops kept in 'cut and spread' condition in the field
Add-on/Index-based covers for specific risks that states can offer optionally (e.g., wild animal attack, drought spell index)

concepts.name: Sum Insured and Scale of Finance Concept
key_dimensions: Sum insured equals Scale of Finance (SoF) per hectare as fixed by the District Level Technical Committee (DLTC)
Scale of Finance determination: who decides it and how — DLTC chaired by Lead District Manager (LDM)
Difference between Sum Insured under PMFBY vs. MNAIS — PMFBY uses SoF, not market value of produce
Dispute: underinsurance problem when SoF is lower than actual cost of cultivation — farmer grievance angle

concepts.name: Unit of Insurance and Crop-Cutting Experiments (CCEs)
key_dimensions: Basic unit: Village/Village Panchayat level for major crops; higher for others — shift from taluka/block level under NAIS (UPSC trap)
Crop Cutting Experiments (CCEs): purpose, methodology, who conducts them (State Agriculture Dept), and their role in yield estimation
Technology integration: mandatory use of smartphones, CCE-Agri app, drones to reduce CCE manipulation and delays
Delay in CCE data submission by states — principal reason for delayed claim settlements, leading to farmer dissatisfaction

concepts.name: Claim Settlement Mechanism and Timelines
key_dimensions: Mandated timeline: claims to be settled within 2 months of harvest; advance payment of 25% for mid-season adversity on ad-hoc basis
Account-based direct transfer: claims credited directly to farmer's bank account (DBT) — Aadhaar seeding requirement
Penalty on insurance companies for delayed payment: 12% per annum interest payable to farmers — rarely enforced (governance gap)
Dispute resolution: District Grievance Redressal Committee (DGRC) → State → IRDAI arbitration pathway

concepts.name: Role of Implementing Agencies — Insurance Companies
key_dimensions: Both public sector (AIC — Agriculture Insurance Company of India) and private insurers empaneled — IRDAI regulation applies
Empanelment process: multi-year contracts awarded by states through competitive bidding — tension between cost minimization and service quality
AIC of India: its unique status as a specialized agricultural insurer under DAC&FW — not a general insurer (UPSC trap)
Windfall profit controversy: insurers collecting high actuarial premiums in good years vs. underpaying claims — calls for profit-sharing or loss-sharing caps

concepts.name: Technology Integration: PMFBY Tech Ecosystem
key_dimensions: NCIP (National Crop Insurance Portal): centralized platform for enrollment, premium collection, and claim processing — single-window
Fasal Bima App: farmer-facing app for enrollment, claim intimation within 72 hours of localized loss — UPSC may ask about the 72-hour rule
Use of Remote Sensing, Satellite Imagery, and Drones for yield estimation — reducing dependence on physical CCEs
Bhuvan portal (ISRO) integration and Weather Information Network Data Systems (WINDS) for weather-based triggers

concepts.name: PMFBY vs. Weather Based Crop Insurance Scheme (WBCIS) — Comparative
key_dimensions: PMFBY: yield-index based (actual yield vs. threshold yield); WBCIS: weather-index based (deviation from weather parameters) — fundamental structural difference
Basis risk: higher in WBCIS (individual farm loss may not correlate with weather index) vs. lower in PMFBY — but CCE delays plague PMFBY
Premium structure: both have same farmer-payable caps (2%, 1.5%, 5%) — UPSC trap: students assume WBCIS has different caps
WBCIS administered by same agencies (AIC + private insurers) but uses Automatic Weather Stations (AWS) as reference units

concepts.name: Fiscal Federalism Issues — State Opt-Outs and Participation
key_dimensions: States that withdrew from PMFBY: Bihar (2018), West Bengal (2019), Andhra Pradesh, Telangana, Jharkhand — reasons (premium burden, political choice for own schemes)
States launching alternate schemes: Bihar's own crop assistance scheme (Rajya Fasal Sahayata Yojana) — input subsidy model vs. insurance model comparison
Centre's response: states free to opt out but lose access to central premium subsidy; no coercion — cooperative federalism tension
Premium arrears problem: states delaying their share of premium subsidy payment to insurers, blocking farmer claims — accountability gap

concepts.name: Enrollment Coverage and Inclusion Gaps
key_dimensions: Non-loanee farmers: historically underrepresented despite being the intended beneficiaries — enrollment largely driven by loanee farmers pre-2020
Tenant farmers and sharecroppers: eligible but face documentation barriers (land records not in their name) — policy says notional coverage but ground reality differs
Landless agricultural laborers: NOT covered under PMFBY — a deliberate exclusion (UPSC trap: students assume all farming community is covered)
Geographic exclusion: North-East states' low participation despite favorable 90:10 subsidy ratio — infrastructural and administrative reasons

concepts.name: Notified Crops and Area Limitation
key_dimensions: Only 'notified crops' in 'notified areas' are covered — not all crops everywhere; state decides which crops to notify
This creates a coverage gap: farmer growing a non-notified crop in a notified area or vice versa is excluded
Horticulture and commercial crops: covered at 5% premium cap but historically under-notified by states due to complex valuation
Perennial crops and plantation crops: largely outside PMFBY scope — separate schemes (e.g., Coconut Palm Insurance Scheme) handle them

concepts.name: Structural Critique: Actuarial Model vs. Social Protection Model
key_dimensions: PMFBY uses actuarial pricing (insurer charges real risk-based premium, government subsidizes) vs. NAIS's flat subsidized premium — philosophical difference
Criticism: benefits accrue more to insurers than farmers in low-claim years — profit asymmetry argument
Counter-argument: actuarial model ensures long-term financial viability of insurance; NAIS was fiscally unsustainable
Recommendations: Standing Committee on Agriculture, CAG reports, and Ramesh Chand Committee suggestions for structural overhaul — moving toward a re-insurance or government-as-insurer model

concepts.name: Prevented Sowing / Planting Cover
key_dimensions: Triggered when widespread calamity prevents more than 75% of farmers in a notified unit from sowing — threshold is critical (UPSC trap on the 75% figure)
Coverage amount: up to 25% of sum insured paid as indemnity — not full coverage
Distinction from 'localized calamity' cover: prevented sowing is area-wide; localized is farm-specific (hailstorm, landslide)
Assessment method: based on area sown data from state revenue/agriculture department, not CCE — different data source than yield-loss claims

concepts.name: Mid-Season Adversity Provision
key_dimensions: Triggered when expected yield is less than 50% of normal yield due to adverse conditions during the crop season
Advance payment: up to 25% of likely claims released immediately without waiting for harvest/CCE — unique feature of PMFBY not present in NAIS
Assessment: done through remote sensing/satellite data or field reports, not full CCE — faster but less precise
Reconciliation: advance payment is adjusted against final claim — if final claim is lower, no recovery from farmer (pro-farmer design)

concepts.name: Institutional Architecture: NMCFC and Governance Structure
key_dimensions: National Level: DAC&FW (Department of Agriculture, Cooperation & Farmers Welfare) is the nodal ministry
NMCFC (National Monitoring Committee for Fasal Bima): chaired by Agriculture Secretary — oversight body for PMFBY and WBCIS
State Level: State Level Coordination Committee on Crop Insurance (SLCCCI) — implementation and dispute coordination
District Level: DLTC (District Level Technical Committee) — fixes Scale of Finance, notifies crops, oversees CCEs; LDM is the chair (UPSC trap: not Collector)

concepts.name: CAG and Parliamentary Committee Findings on PMFBY
key_dimensions: CAG Report (2017): found delays in claim settlement, overestimation of premiums by insurers, and states not releasing subsidy on time
Parliamentary Standing Committee observations: demanded profit-sharing clause, cap on insurer margins, and penalty enforcement
Key metric controversy: government claims rising gross premiums as success; critics say low claim ratios (claims paid / premiums collected) indicate poor value for farmers
Reforms triggered: 2020 revamp making it voluntary, introducing penalty clauses, and mandating technology use — direct policy response to audit findings

concepts.name: PMFBY and Climate Change / Disaster Risk Reduction Linkage
key_dimensions: PMFBY as a component of India's climate adaptation strategy — recognized in National Action Plan on Climate Change (NAPCC) framework
Increasing frequency of extreme weather events (unseasonal rain, cyclones) expanding potential claim pool — fiscal sustainability concern
Index-based insurance as a scalable climate-resilience tool: WBCIS more adaptable to climate parameters than yield-based PMFBY
Integration with PM-KISAN and soil health card data being explored to create a comprehensive farmer risk-profiling system

concepts.name: Comparison with Global Crop Insurance Models
key_dimensions: USA's FCIC/RMA model: federally reinsured, private delivery, revenue insurance (not just yield) — India lacks revenue insurance component
China's model: rapid expansion via subsidized premiums, strong local government involvement — similar premium subsidy architecture to India
Africa/developing world: index-based microinsurance more prevalent due to weak land records — India's CCE-based model is more robust but costly
UPSC angle: India's model is actuarial + subsidy hybrid; purely index-based or purely government-run models are the two alternatives debated for India's reform
